title: The World of AI: Robotics Models catalogue page
answer: The World of AI publishes this catalogue page for Robotics Models. It describes a list of the 1000 most downloaded open robotics models on the Hugging Face Hub, with licence, downloads, and release date, refreshed daily. The most useful point is that the list is built from the Hugging Face Hub public API, sorted by all time downloads, and every model links to its own Hub page. It also references vision language action models, though the text is truncated.

sections.body: The World of AI publishes this page as a catalogue entry for Robotics Models. It says the page covers the 1000 most downloaded open robotics models on the Hugging Face Hub, with licence, downloads, and release date, refreshed daily. The stated source is the Hugging Face Hub public API, sorted by all time downloads, refreshed daily, and every model links to its own Hub page. The page carries a last verified date of 2026-09-28. It also includes site search information, a citation line, promotional notes about books and consulting services, and a description of the site as an atlas of artificial intelligence.
sections.heading: What this source is

sections.body: The page states that it catalogues the 1000 most downloaded open robotics models on the Hugging Face Hub. For each model it lists licence, downloads, and release date, and the list is refreshed daily. The ranking comes from the Hugging Face Hub public API and is sorted by all time downloads. Every model links to its own Hub page. The text also begins to mention vision language action models, but the phrase is cut off in the harvested text. Beyond the robotics list, the page describes a site wide search that covers the full text of every published page, all built from the same database. That database includes state AI laws, a lawsuit tracker, a glossary, a tools directory, AI companies, a research library, an MCP server registry, compliance frameworks, sources, people, calculators, and weekly digests. The page says it was last verified on 2026-09-28. It gives a citation format for the page. It also carries promotional material: books by Stephen R. Jordan, including The Operating Discipline for AI Library series, are said to be available on Amazon, and SRJ Consulting & Services has published a novel called The AI Lawyer, out 17 August 2026. The page lists several audit and assessment services. It describes the wider site as an atlas of artificial intelligence covering what the law says, who is suing whom, and what the words mean, rebuilt daily from primary sources, free to read, free to cite, and free to query.
sections.heading: What it says

sections.body: The source states that the list covers the 1000 most downloaded open robotics models on the Hugging Face Hub. It says the data comes from the Hugging Face Hub public API, is sorted by all time downloads, and is refreshed daily. It states that each model entry includes licence, downloads, and release date, and that every model links to its own Hub page. It gives a last verified date of 2026-09-28. It says The AI Lawyer is out 17 August 2026. It also uses the term vision language action, but the phrase is truncated. The text gives no transportation specific figures.
sections.heading: Figures and claims worth noting

sections.body: A reader following AI in transportation can use this source as a pointer to a daily updated catalogue of open robotics models, including vision language action models, which may be relevant to robotics and embodied systems in transport. The page itself does not discuss transportation use cases, deployment, safety, or regulation. Its value is mainly as an index: it shows which open robotics models are most downloaded on the Hugging Face Hub and provides licence, download, and release date metadata, with links to each model page. For someone tracking AI in transportation, that can help identify widely used open models, but it is not evidence about transport performance or suitability.
sections.heading: What it means for AI in Transportation

sections.body: This is a catalogue and landing page with little substantive analysis. It does not cover transportation applications, model performance, safety, or real world deployment. It relies on Hugging Face Hub download counts as a ranking and does not explain that choice beyond saying the list is sorted by all time downloads. Parts of the page are promotional, including books by Stephen R. Jordan, SRJ Consulting & Services, and a list of audit and assessment services. The vision language action phrase is truncated in the harvested text. The page is dated 2026-09-28 and is not a research report, policy document, or independent evaluation.
